NewPlanInput.description:
Input for `routing24_new_plan`: commit a fresh EMPTY plan, replacing the
loaded one (the app asks the user to confirm when the loaded plan holds
data, and unsaved changes are auto-saved first). Follow with the
`routing24_upsert_*` tools to create the depot/vehicles/stops, then solve
with `routing24_reoptimize_plan`.

planUuid.description:
The plan the call acted on. EXTERNAL (MCP) surface only — the in-app
chat drives one loaded plan, so the handler omits it there. A handle in
a result reads to a weak model as a handle to pass back: one echoed it
into every following call and spent the turn on unknown-field
rejections (llm-planuuid-err). No input anywhere takes it.

NewPlanResult.description: Result of `routing24_new_plan`: the fresh empty plan is now the loaded one.

planUuid.description:
The plan the call acted on. EXTERNAL (MCP) surface only — the in-app
chat drives one loaded plan, so the handler omits it there. A handle in
a result reads to a weak model as a handle to pass back: one echoed it
into every following call and spent the turn on unknown-field
rejections (llm-planuuid-err). No input anywhere takes it.

solveRun.description:
1-based counter of solve launches in this session. Each launch is a NEW
run even when the request repeats — two identical re-optimizes are two
distinct solves, and this field is what makes their results distinct.

paidFeatures.description: Present only when the plan uses paid features outside this account.

warnings.description:
Non-blocking notes about how the request was interpreted (e.g. an
all-zero cost model replaced by the default rates of 1 per mile/km
plus 1 per hour). Omitted when there is nothing to say.

timeLimitS.description:
The solver's time budget for this run, in seconds (`options.time_limit_s`
or the size-based default). Geocoding and matrix time come on top, so the
run lands shortly after this many seconds of solving.

SolveStarted.description: Result of `routing24_reoptimize_plan`: the solve is running, poll for progress.

locked.description:
Paid capabilities the plan uses that this account's plan does not
include, as `Feature` member names (e.g. `"Skills"`, `"DriverBreaks"`).

stripped.description:
The subset DROPPED from this solve because the free allowance for paid
features is spent. Empty while the allowance lasts. A non-empty list
means the routes ignore those constraints — say so when reporting the
plan, and name the upgrade as the way to get them back.

freeRunsLeft.description: Free solves left that may use locked features (0 once spent).

PaidFeatureReport.description:
What the solve did with the paid features the plan uses. Absent when the
plan uses none, or when every one of them is included in the user's
subscription — the common case, and nothing to report.

unassignedSummary.description:
One-line WHY for a nonzero `unassignedCount` (from the last computed
diagnostics), so every status poll keeps the reasons one hop away. The
per-stop reasons, numeric targets and fixes come from
`routing24_unassigned`.

problemsCount.description: Total constraint-problem markers across all routes (0 = feasible).

driftFromOptimized.description: Drift vs the last full optimization (absent while a solve runs).

planUuid.description:
The plan the call acted on. EXTERNAL (MCP) surface only — the in-app
chat drives one loaded plan, so the handler omits it there. A handle in
a result reads to a weak model as a handle to pass back: one echoed it
into every following call and spent the turn on unknown-field
rejections (llm-planuuid-err). No input anywhere takes it.

complete.description: True when the solve ran to completion (not cancelled part-way).

cost.description:
Economic cost (money) of the whole plan. Coverage is `unassignedCount`,
never a cost. Absent on pre-feature solutions.

objective.description: Solver comparison scalar — see {@link SolverObjective}; never money.

costModel.description:
The per-unit pricing this solve used, fallbacks included — see
{@link CostModel}. Absent mid-solve and on pre-feature solutions.

routeStats.description:
One compact entry per route (empty routes included), in on-screen order:
vehicle, stop count, distance, duration, feasibility and cost per route —
NO stop list. Drill into one route's ordered stops with `routing24_route`.

revision.description:
Session revision the routes reflect (present once an editing session is
open); bumps on every committed edit.

dataSync.description:
Present ONLY when the plan data (or the distance unit) changed after
the last optimization — see {@link DataSyncStatus}.

rev.description:
Plan drift counter: bumps on EVERY recorded plan mutation (yours, the
user's, another assistant's). Moved since your last call and
`lastEditBy` isn't you → re-read before editing. Tab-session-scoped:
going backwards also means re-read.

optimizedAt.description: When the baseline solve completed (ms since epoch).

distancePct.description: Travel-distance change vs the baseline, percent (+ = longer).

durationPct.description: Total-duration change vs the baseline, percent (+ = slower).

cost.description:
ECONOMIC cost change, money (+ = more expensive). Coverage drift is
`unassigned` (a count) — the two are never merged into one number.
Absent when the baseline carried no cost.

costPct.description: Cost change vs the baseline, percent (+ = more expensive).

problems.description: New problem markers vs the baseline (+ = worse).

unassigned.description: Newly unassigned stops vs the baseline (+ = worse).

severity.description:
Fixed-threshold verdict: any new problem/unassigned ⇒ at least
`degraded`; cost, distance or duration > +5% ⇒ `degraded`, > +15% ⇒
`severe`; everything ≤ baseline with a ≥1% gain ⇒ `improved`; else
`neutral`.

summary.description: One ready-to-quote sentence, lexicographic: coverage first, then money.

OptimizedDrift.description:
How far the CURRENT plan has drifted from the last full optimization —
covering every change since that solve, the user's manual edits included.
Recompute-free: the baseline is frozen at solve completion; only a new
`routing24_reoptimize_plan` (or the user's OPTIMIZE button) resets it. Absent when
the plan predates the baseline feature or was never solved.

REPORTING OBLIGATION: when `severity` is `degraded` or `severe`, tell the
user (quote `summary`) and stop there. An edit the user asked for is
expected to cost more — never re-optimize (or propose it) to walk one back;
re-optimizing is only ever the user's own request.

components.description:
The solver's own decomposition of `total` — every charged line, zero
lines omitted. Plan-level lines carry amounts and plan-wide quantities
but NO rates (rates can differ per vehicle — read
`OptimizeStatus.costModel`, or one route's cost from `routing24_route`,
for rate-level verification).

SolutionCost.description:
ECONOMIC cost of the solution, in the task's money units (the unit costs
configured on the vehicles). Report money to the user from here. It does
NOT include unassigned-order penalties — coverage is a count
(`unassignedCount`), not a cost. Absent on pre-feature solutions.

amount.description: Money — an addend of the parent `total`. Report this.

rate.description:
Effective per-`unit` rate the solve used (on `routing24_route` costs
only) — the authored rate at the engine's fixed-point step (1e-6 per
wire unit), rounded to 2 decimals here, so it normally equals the
vehicle's configured value. See `defaultRate` before presenting it as
configured.

unit.description:
Unit of `quantity` (and denominator of `rate`). Distance units are the
SOLVE-TIME display unit; `load-mi`/`load-km` = load unit × mile/km.

defaultRate.description:
The `rate` is an engine DEFAULT — the matching vehicle cost field is
blank in the app, the engine supplied the value (see
{@link VehicleEffectiveRates}.`defaultRates`). Call it a default;
never present it as a cost the user configured.

CostComponent.description:
One line of a cost total. Self-describing: a future pricing element arrives
as a new `kind`, never a new shape. `amount` is the solver's authoritative
money value; when `rate` and `quantity` are present, `amount` ≈ `rate` ×
`quantity` (2-decimal rounding; a force-placed stop on a restricted leg may
legitimately price below that — `amount` wins).

unassignedPenalty.description: Σ synthetic penalties of unassigned orders (incl. alternatives not chosen).

SolverObjective.description:
The scalar the solver minimizes — SOLVER UNITS, NOT MONEY, never quote it
to the user. Each unassigned order carries a synthetic penalty priced
above any possible serving cost, so fewer-unassigned always outranks
cheaper-routes. Use it ONLY to compare two states of the same plan:
lower `objective.total` = better plan. Equivalent hand rule: fewer
unassigned wins; ties break on lower `cost.total`.

note.description: Ready-to-quote explanation, present when `priced` is false.

distanceUnit.description: Solve-time display distance unit the rates are stated in.

vehicles.description: Effective per-unit rates per vehicle type.

CostModel.description:
The pricing this solve ACTUALLY used — the vehicles' authored cost rates
after the engine's fallbacks. `priced: false` means NO vehicle prices
distance, duration or load-distance: the optimizer then minimizes distance
and time together (every vehicle priced at the defaults of 1 per mile/km
plus 1 per hour), so `cost.total` reads roughly as the plan's travel
distance in miles/km plus its total route time in hours (driving + service
+ waiting) — quote `note` when explaining. Absent on pre-feature solutions.

defaultRates.description:
Rates the ENGINE supplied — the vehicle's matching cost field is blank
in the app: `distance` and `duration` when the fleet is unpriced (the
defaults of 1 per mile/km and 1 per hour), `overtime` when overtime is
allowed but unpriced (priced at the vehicle's hourly rate, else a
nominal 1/hour). Call these defaults; never present one as a cost the
user configured.

VehicleEffectiveRates.description:
One vehicle type's effective rates, in `CostModel.distanceUnit` and hours:
`fixed` per route driven, `distance` per mi/km, `duration` / `overtime` /
`rideOvertime` per hour, `stop` per stop served, `loadDistance` per load
unit per mi/km. An omitted rate = 0 (not charged). Rates are what the
engine BILLS — the authored value at the engine's fixed-point step (1e-6
per wire unit), rounded to 2 decimals here, so a rate normally equals the
authored one; the authored values themselves are on the vehicle rows
(`routing24_list_vehicles`).

cost.description: Economic cost of this route (absent on pre-feature solutions).

distance.description: Total travel distance of the route, in `distanceUnit`.

route.description:
1-based route number, matching the on-screen order — the SAME number
every route-addressed tool takes (`routing24_route`,
`routing24_reoptimize_route`, the `routing24_edit_*` `to_route`/`route`/
`target`/`sources` fields). Numbers renumber after
`routing24_edit_remove_routes`;
re-read them from the returned state.

vehicleId.description: Id of the vehicle serving this route.

stopCount.description: Count of site stops served (the depot start/end are excluded).

durationHours.description: Total route duration (travel + service + wait), hours.

feasible.description: True when every constraint on this route is satisfied.

breakCount.description:
Scheduled driver-break stops on this route (they appear in `stops`
with type `break`). Absent = none — legitimate when the route's total
driving stays under the rule's trigger.

breakDurationS.description: Total scheduled break time on this route, seconds. Absent = none.

problemsCount.description:
Constraint-problem markers on this route (0 = feasible); read the
problems themselves from `routing24_route`.

RouteBrief.description:
One route's compact stats in {@link OptimizeStatus}.`routeStats` — totals
only, no stop list. Drill into the ordered stops with `routing24_route(route)`.
The shared fields are {@link PlanSolutionRoute}'s, defined once there —
`breakCount`/`breakDurationS` included, so "which routes have driver
breaks" is answerable from `routing24_status` alone.

RouteCost.description:
One route's ECONOMIC cost, in the task's money units. `total` =
Σ `components[].amount`. In `routeStats` and session route summaries the
lines carry amounts only; `routing24_route` adds the serving vehicle's
effective `rate`/`quantity`/`unit` per line.

distanceUnitChanged.description:
The display distance unit changed since the solve (miles <-> km), which
alone re-prices the solution's distances.

DataSyncStatus.description:
What changed in the plan data AFTER the last optimization — the same
condition that shows the user the NOT SYNC badge. The current solution and
the route-editing tools still see the plan as of that solve; the changes
counted here take effect on the next optimization (run it only when the
user asks). A kind that is absent is unchanged.

EntityKindDiff.description:
Counts of one entity kind's rows that differ from the last optimization's
snapshot of the plan.

route.description:
1-based route number from `OptimizeStatus.routeStats[].route` — the
same number shown to the user (Route 1 = `route: 1`).

RouteInput.description:
Input for `routing24_route`: one route's full detail by its 1-based `route`
number.

route.description:
1-based route number, matching the on-screen order — the SAME number
every route-addressed tool takes (`routing24_route`,
`routing24_reoptimize_route`, the `routing24_edit_*` `to_route`/`route`/
`target`/`sources` fields). Numbers renumber after
`routing24_edit_remove_routes`;
re-read them from the returned state.

vehicleId.description: Id of the vehicle serving this route.

stopCount.description: Count of site stops served (the depot start/end are excluded).

distance.description: Total travel distance of the route, in `distanceUnit`.

durationHours.description: Total route duration (travel + service + wait), hours.

startTimeS.description:
When the route starts (depot departure, or arrival at the first
order on an open-start route), seconds since midnight.

endTimeS.description:
When the route ends (depot return, or service completion at the last
order on an open-ended route), seconds since midnight.

feasible.description: True when every constraint on this route is satisfied.

cost.description: Economic cost of this route (absent on pre-feature solutions).

stops.description:
Stops in visit order; bounded by depot stops unless the vehicle's
start/finish depot is empty (open-ended).

breakCount.description:
Scheduled driver-break stops on this route (they appear in `stops`
with type `break`). Absent = none — legitimate when the route's total
driving stays under the rule's trigger.

breakDurationS.description: Total scheduled break time on this route, seconds. Absent = none.

PlanSolutionRoute.description:
One route: an ordered stop sequence, bounded by depot stops when the
vehicle has a start/finish depot (open-ended ends start/finish at an order
instead). Empty routes (a vehicle with no stops, e.g. just created by
`routing24_edit_create_route`) are included with `stopCount: 0` so `route` stays a
complete, editable address space.

amount.description: How far over the constraint (see {@link PlanProblemType} for units).

PlanProblemType.description:
Constraint kinds a problem can report (common.fbs `ConstraintType`).
`amount` units: seconds for the time kinds, load units for `capacity`,
distance for `max_distance`.

seq.description: 0-based position within the route (0 = the starting depot).

type.description:
The depot, a delivery/pickup site, or a scheduled driver break. A
`break` stop is a solver-planned pause taken AT the previous stop's
location: it has no `id`/`address`, `serviceDurationS` is the pause
length, and its travel-leg fields are 0. These stops are the ONLY
break credit: a `waitDurationS` on an ordinary stop is idle time that
does NOT count toward the driver-break rules (unless the rule sets
`service_counts`), so never present a wait as a break.

id.description: The site/depot id (the id you passed to optimize, or an auto-assigned one).

arrivalTimeS.description: Arrival time, seconds since midnight (physical driver timeline).

departureTimeS.description: End of service (arrival + wait + service), seconds since midnight.

serviceDurationS.description: Time spent servicing this stop, seconds.

waitDurationS.description: Wait before the stop's time window opens, seconds (0/absent = none).

legDistance.description: Distance of the travel leg arriving at this stop, in `distanceUnit`.

legDurationS.description: Duration of the travel leg arriving at this stop, seconds.

pickedUpLoad.description: Load picked up at this stop.

problems.description: Constraint problems materializing at this stop (absent = none).

marginalCost.description:
Removal saving — how much cheaper (money) / shorter (seconds) this
route gets without this stop, same vehicle kept. An estimate for the
CURRENT stop order: savings are NOT additive across stops and change
after any edit or re-optimize. Absent on depots and pre-feature plans.

refresh_diagnostics.description:
Recompute the unassigned-site diagnostics before returning them (runs an
engine pass; only needed when `diagnosticsStale` was true).

available.description: `false` when the loaded plan carries no optimized solution yet.

unassignedCount.description: Number of site stops that could not be served.

unassigned.description: Ids of the unassigned sites, if any.

alternativesNotChosen.description:
Group-alternative sites not chosen (a sibling serves the group) — these
are NOT failures.

userUnassigned.description: Unassigned site ids that were removed by the user/agent (not the solver).

diagnosticsStale.description:
True when `unassignedDiagnostics` predates the latest edits — pass
`refresh_diagnostics: true` to recompute before reading it.

unassignedDiagnostics.description: Why sites are unassigned, in prose (capped; see `truncated`/`omitted`).

insertionQuotes.description:
Ready-to-serve quotes for the unassigned orders (the cheapest feasible
placement for each quotable site; none when nothing fits). Refreshed with
the diagnostics — pass `refresh_diagnostics: true` when `diagnosticsStale`.

UnassignedReport.description:
Result of `routing24_unassigned`: which sites of the loaded plan are unserved
and why. `available` is `false` when the plan has no solution yet.

summary.description: One-paragraph overview of the unassigned situation.

truncated.description: True when the per-site list was capped (see `omitted`).

category.description: Coarse cause (e.g. hard incompatibility vs fleet contention).

blockers.description: Site ids standing in the way (competition for the same capacity).

levers.description: Constraint changes that would let this site be served.

omitted.description: Rollup of the sites the cap left out.

UnassignedDiagnosticsReport.description:
Prose explanation of why sites are unassigned (common.fbs
`UnassignedDiagnosticsLlm` — the agent-facing projection, capped in size).

route.description: 1-based route number of the quoted insertion point.

deliveryAfter.description:
Pair quote (stop = the pickup): where the DELIVERY step is quoted, after
the pickup (precedence-aware). Absent for a single order.

InsertionQuote.description:
The cheapest FEASIBLE way to serve one unassigned order in the current
routes — REAL units (money / seconds), safe to quote to the user. Directly
replayable with `routing24_edit_move_stops`: use `before`/`after` as the anchor (or
`to_route: route` with `placement: "best"` when both are absent).
`route` absent = a spare `vehicleId` vehicle serves it on a fresh
single-visit route, its fixed cost included (an existing route's fixed
cost is sunk and excluded). Estimates for the CURRENT arrangement only:
quotes are NOT additive across orders and go stale with any edit or
re-optimize (`diagnosticsStale`).

stops.description: Stop business ids to move, kept together as one block.

before.description: Anchor stop id: insert the block immediately before it.

after.description: Anchor stop id: insert the block immediately after it.

placement.description: With `to_route`: `append` to the end, or `best` = cheapest insertion.

user_assigned.description: Mark the stops user-assigned (badge + problem report). Default true.

EditMoveStopsInput.description:
Input for `routing24_edit_move_stops`: move/re-plan planned OR unassigned
stops. Anchor with `before`/`after` (a planned stop id on the destination
route), or target a route with `to_route` + `placement`.

stops.description: Stop business ids to remove from their routes.

user_unassigned.description:
Stamp the "removed by you" marker (default true). Pass false to unassign
without claiming the removal, keeping the stop's original reason.

vehicle.description: Vehicle id; rejects `vehicle_overused` when its count is exhausted.
Vehicle id for the new empty route (appended last).

routes.description:
Route numbers (1-based) to delete. The remaining routes renumber —
re-read them after.

EditRemoveRoutesInput.description:
Input for `routing24_edit_remove_routes`. The stops on those routes are
unassigned first, in the SAME atomic batch — the engine's own remove op
accepts empty routes only.

after.description: Stop id that becomes the last stop of the head route.

vehicle.description:
Vehicle for the new tail route. Absent = the source route's own type
while it has an instance left, else an unused one is picked and
reported in `autoPickedVehicle`.

target.description: Route number (1-based) that receives the stops.

sources.description:
Route numbers (1-based) whose stops move onto `target`, left empty
afterwards.

applied.description: True when the whole batch committed; false = nothing was applied.

rejection.description: Why the batch rolled back (all-or-nothing), when the engine rejected it.

state.description: Current state — post-apply, or unchanged when the batch was rejected.

userAssignedReports.description: Problem reports for all currently user-assigned sites (when `applied`).

autoPickedVehicle.description:
Present when the tool had to choose a vehicle the input did not name —
see {@link AutoPickedVehicle}. Say so in your answer.

reason.description: Human-readable rejection detail, when the engine supplies one.

EditOpStatus.description: The rejected op of a failed batch (edits.fbs `EditStatus`).

EditRejectionCode.description:
Why an edit batch was rejected (edits.fbs `EditRejection`, minus `none`).
Notable: `stale_revision` = the plan changed under you — re-read
`routing24_status` and rebuild the batch; `optimize_in_progress` = wait for
the running optimization; `slot_out_of_range`/`overlapping_slots` mean your
route numbers are outdated.

problemsCount.description: Total constraint-problem markers across all routes (0 = feasible).

unassigned.description: Ids of the sites currently unassigned.

cost.description: Economic cost (money). Coverage is `unassignedCount`, never a cost.

objective.description: Solver comparison scalar — see {@link SolverObjective}; never money.

routes.description: Every route, fresh — supersedes route numbers from before the mutation.

unusedVehicles.description:
Vehicle types with a free instance — the fleet a new route can still be
given. Absent = every instance is bound to a route; another route then
needs one freed (`routing24_edit_remove_routes` /
`routing24_edit_merge_routes`) or a re-optimize with a bigger fleet,
because a vehicle ADDED to the plan now only becomes usable on the next
optimization.

driftFromOptimized.description: Drift vs the last full optimization — report `degraded`/`severe`.

SessionState.description: Post-mutation session snapshot shared by the editing tools' results.

route.description: 1-based route number (fresh — valid for the next edit call).

stops.description:
Ordered site ids (depots and driver breaks excluded — breaks have no
id; see `breakCount` and `routing24_route` for them).

cost.description: Economic cost of this route (absent on pre-feature solutions).

breakCount.description: Scheduled driver-break stops on this route. Absent = none.

breakDurationS.description: Total scheduled break time on this route, seconds. Absent = none.

RouteSummary.description: One route's summary in a {@link SessionState} (post-edit snapshot).

count.description: Instances free to take one more route.

UnusedVehicle.description:
A vehicle type this session has instances left of. Each route binds one
instance for as long as the route exists (EMPTY routes included), so this
is what a NEW route can be given — the tail of `routing24_edit_split_route`,
`routing24_edit_create_route`, or the target of
`routing24_edit_set_route_vehicle`. Shown to the user as "Unused vehicles".

route.description: Route number (1-based) the stop sits on.

UserAssignedProblemReport.description:
The problem report behind a user-assigned site's badge (edits.fbs
`UserAssignedReport`): what placing it costs, split into problems the site
would have anywhere (`intrinsic`) vs ones this placement introduced.

route.description: 1-based number of the route the picked vehicle now serves.

insteadOf.description: The vehicle it would have used, had that type had an instance left.

AutoPickedVehicle.description:
A vehicle the tool picked itself. `routing24_edit_split_route` gives the
tail the source route's own vehicle type by default; when that type has no
instance left, an unused one is taken instead rather than failing the split.
The tail therefore runs a DIFFERENT vehicle than the head — different
capacity, shift and cost — so tell the user which one it got.

route.description:
Route number to optimize — 1-based, as in
`OptimizeStatus.routeStats[].route` and the UI; needs ≥2 stops.

time_limit_s.description: Wall budget in seconds; omit to auto-scale with route size (1.5–5s).

ReoptimizeRouteInput.description: Input for `routing24_reoptimize_route`: re-sequence ONE route's stops.

started.description: False when the run could not start (see `errorCode`/`error`).

query.description: Case-insensitive substring over the id and address fields.

offset.description: 0-based row offset into the filtered list.

ListPageInput.description:
Input for the four `routing24_list_*` tools — one paging/filter shape, and
each tool returns ONE row type. (A single list tool taking a `kind` would
switch its own result shape, so a caller could not know what it would get
back without re-reading the input it had just sent.)

total.description: Rows matching the filter, before paging.

ListStopsResult.description:
Result of `routing24_list_stops`. Rows use the SAME shape
`routing24_upsert_stops` accepts, so read-modify-write needs no field
mapping — including `area`.

address.description:
The WHOLE place the user named, spelling fixed — every part they wrote
(building, tower, unit, street). Order words riding in the same line
("pickup 2", a quantity) are NOT part of the address and never become
one: they belong in the load fields. A decimal "lat, lng" literal
("25.19882, 55.27939") is a valid address: it pins that exact point,
skips the geocoder and stays the row's label.

area.description:
Optional area/city qualifier shown after the address (the address book's
`address`+`area` identity). The `routing24_list_*` tools return it on
every stop/depot row, so accepting it here is what makes that row
writable back through `routing24_upsert_stops`/`_depots` unchanged.

tw_early_s.description: Window opens, seconds since midnight. Absent = opens with the day.

tw_late_s.description:
Window closes, seconds since midnight. Absent = open-ended (no
closing bound on this stop).

delivery.description:
Load DELIVERED to this stop (loaded at the depot, dropped here): a
bare number, or an array of per-unit entries — `[{"unit": "kg",
"value": 300}, {"unit": "pallets", "value": 2}]` — once the plan
names units. A unit you omit keeps its current value; value 0 zeroes
it.

pickup.description:
Load PICKED UP at this stop (taken on here, carried back to the depot
— or, on a transfer pickup end, to the linked delivery). Same number-
or-entries form as `delivery`.

id.description:
Caller-chosen business id — the name every other tool refers to,
and REQUIRED on every upsert row (it is the upsert key). ONE row per
order: never a dumping ground for leftover words (a load like
"pickup 1" is the `pickup` field, not an id and not a second stop,
and an id belongs in this field, never inside `address`).

status.description:
Whether the row's address resolved to a map location. Reported on
`routing24_list_stops` rows; accepted and ignored on upsert (so a
listed row writes back unchanged).

StopRow.description:
A delivery/pickup stop: a place plus solver site constraints.

The intersection above is flattened in the generated schema, which drops the
doc comments of the types it merges — and the schema is all a tool caller
sees, so the conventions those types state are repeated here:
the location is the `address` string, geocoded internally; `id` is the
business id the caller chooses and every other tool refers to (there is no
name field); loads go in `delivery` (loaded at the depot, dropped here) and
`pickup` (taken on here, carried back to the depot); every `*_s` time field
is in seconds — `tw_early_s`/`tw_late_s`/`release_time_s` counted from
midnight, `service_duration_s` a duration.

unit.description:
A declared load unit's name, VERBATIM as the user wrote it ("kg"
stays "kg" — never paraphrased into "weight").

UnitLoad.description: One per-unit load amount in a `delivery`/`pickup`/`capacity` entry array.

total.description: Rows matching the filter, before paging.

tw_early_s.description: Shift starts, seconds since midnight. Absent = no earliest start.

tw_late_s.description:
Shift ends, seconds since midnight. Absent = open-ended: no
shift-end limit at all, the strongest relaxation of the shift.

start_late_s.description:
Latest time the vehicle may start its shift (leave the depot),
distinct from tw_late_s (latest shift end). Absent = defaults to
tw_late_s solver-side.

max_duration_s.description: Max route duration, seconds. Absent = uncapped.

max_distance.description: Max route distance in the plan's display unit. Absent = uncapped.

capacity.description:
What one vehicle of this type carries, in the same units as the stops'
loads: a bare number, or an array of per-unit entries (`[{"unit":
"pallets", "value": 10}, {"unit": "kg", "value": 800}]`) once the
plan names units. Absent = unlimited.

force_allow_sites.description:
Stop ids this vehicle type may serve even when tags forbid it — a
PERMISSION override, not a reservation: other compatible vehicles can
still take the stop. Precedence per vehicle: force_deny_sites beats
force_allow_sites beats the tag rule. To make a stop exclusive to one
vehicle, use tags (required_tags on the stop + that tag on only this
vehicle) or force_deny_sites on every other vehicle.

force_deny_sites.description: Stop ids this vehicle type must never serve (beats force_allow_sites and tags).

start_depot_id.description: Business id of the start/finish depot (see `routing24_upsert_vehicles`).

VehicleRow.description: A vehicle row: the upsert shape plus the resolved depot business ids.

fixed.description: Cost per use of the vehicle; charged only when it drives a route.

distance.description: Cost per km (or per mile when the plan's display unit is miles).

duration.description: Cost per hour of route time.

stop.description:
Cost per stop served (each order visit; a transfer pair counts its
pickup and delivery separately). Depot and reload visits are free.
No unit conversion: charged per visit in your cost units.

overtime.description:
Surcharge per hour of overtime, paired with the vehicle's
`max_overtime_s` cap. When overtime is allowed and this is unset, it
defaults to the `duration` rate (or a nominal 1/hour if that is 0)
so allowed overtime is never free; an explicit 0 makes it free.

ride_overtime.description:
Cost per hour of a linked (pickup & delivery) order's ride time
inside its overtime band (`max_ride_overtime_s`, past
`max_time_in_vehicle_s`). Unset/0 => that band is free.

load_distance.description:
Cost per unit of load carried per km (or per mile when the plan's
display unit is miles): every leg charges the load on board times
the leg's length, so heavier cargo is priced onto shorter paths
and dropped early. Models load-dependent fuel/energy burn and
refrigerated (cold chain) running cost. Counts toward the fleet's
"priced" signal like `distance`/`duration`. Unset/0 => carriage
is free.

solver.VehicleCost.description:
Per-vehicle cost rates. An omitted field means 0. Exception: when NO
vehicle in the fleet has a nonzero `distance`, `duration` or
`load_distance` rate, the optimizer falls back to the default rates of
1 per km (or mile) plus 1 per hour, minimizing distance and time
together; setting every cost to an explicit 0 triggers the same
fallback plus a warning.
An explicit 0 is meaningful in a mixed fleet (e.g. a bike with free
mileage next to a priced van).

total.description: Rows matching the filter, before paging.

address.description:
The WHOLE place the user named, spelling fixed — every part they wrote
(building, tower, unit, street). Order words riding in the same line
("pickup 2", a quantity) are NOT part of the address and never become
one: they belong in the load fields. A decimal "lat, lng" literal
("25.19882, 55.27939") is a valid address: it pins that exact point,
skips the geocoder and stays the row's label.

area.description:
Optional area/city qualifier shown after the address (the address book's
`address`+`area` identity). The `routing24_list_*` tools return it on
every stop/depot row, so accepting it here is what makes that row
writable back through `routing24_upsert_stops`/`_depots` unchanged.

service_duration_s.description: Handling time at the depot, seconds. Absent = none.

tw_early_s.description: Opens at, seconds since midnight. Absent = open from any time.

tw_late_s.description:
Closes at, seconds since midnight. Absent = open-ended: the depot
never closes and the return-by-close constraint is fully lifted.

DepotRow.description:
A depot row: a place plus depot constraints (open window, handling).
Same conventions as {@link StopRow}: an `address` geocoded internally, a
caller-chosen `id`, `tw_early_s`/`tw_late_s` in seconds since midnight and
`service_duration_s` in seconds. `status` is reported on
`routing24_list_depots` rows; accepted and ignored on upsert.

total.description: Rows matching the filter, before paging.

area.description: Optional area/city qualifier displayed after the address.

status.description:
Whether the row resolved to a map location. Reported on
`routing24_list_addresses` rows; accepted and ignored on upsert.

AddressRow.description: An address row: the upsert shape plus how many entities reference it.

delivery.description:
Load DELIVERED to this stop (loaded at the depot, dropped here): a
bare number, or an array of per-unit entries — `[{"unit": "kg",
"value": 300}, {"unit": "pallets", "value": 2}]` — once the plan
names units. A unit you omit keeps its current value; value 0 zeroes
it.

pickup.description:
Load PICKED UP at this stop (taken on here, carried back to the depot
— or, on a transfer pickup end, to the linked delivery). Same number-
or-entries form as `delivery`.

id.description:
Caller-chosen business id — the name every other tool refers to,
and REQUIRED on every upsert row (it is the upsert key). ONE row per
order: never a dumping ground for leftover words (a load like
"pickup 1" is the `pickup` field, not an id and not a second stop,
and an id belongs in this field, never inside `address`).

status.description:
Whether the row's address resolved to a map location. Reported on
`routing24_list_stops` rows; accepted and ignored on upsert (so a
listed row writes back unchanged).

coordinates.description:
Exact coordinates you already hold, instead of having the `address`
geocoded. The row is placed on this point and the geocoder is not
called, so send only coordinates the user gave you, never remembered
ones. With an `address` too, the address stays the row's label; without
one the label becomes "lat, lng". A decimal "lat, lng" `address` literal
does the same thing. INPUT only: no tool returns coordinates.

Input for `routing24_upsert_vehicles`. `start_depot_id`/`end_depot_id` take
depot business ids and may be omitted when the plan has exactly one depot.

What one vehicle of this type carries, in the same units as the stops'
loads: a bare number, or an array of per-unit entries (`[{"unit":
"pallets", "value": 10}, {"unit": "kg", "value": 800}]`) once the
plan names units. Absent = unlimited.

area.description: Optional area/city qualifier displayed after the address.

status.description:
Whether the row resolved to a map location. Reported on
`routing24_list_addresses` rows; accepted and ignored on upsert.

AddressUpsert.description:
One address-book row for `routing24_upsert_addresses` (and the row shape
`routing24_list_addresses` returns). The row's identity
is the `address` (+ `area`) string pair — upserting the same pair updates
the existing row.

applied.description:
False ONLY when nothing was written. A batch where some rows were
rejected and the rest landed is `true` — read `rejected` for what did
not.

error.description: Why nothing was written; set only when `applied` is false.

skipped.description:
Rows that were NOT written. `added + updated + skipped` always equals
the number of rows you sent.

rejected.description: The skipped rows with the reason each. Capped — see `rejectedOmitted`.

rejectedOmitted.description:
How many skipped rows `rejected` could not carry because of that cap —
so `rejected` is a SAMPLE and every occurrence needs fixing, not just
the listed ones. Absent = `rejected` lists all of them.

warnings.description:
Values dropped from rows that DID land (an unknown id in a reference
list). The row was written without them.

geocoded.description:
How many entities were geocoded from their address on the way in
(rows whose address could not be geocoded are still saved — see
`addressDiagnostics`).

addressDiagnostics.description: Present only when the batch left address problems behind.

fleetDiagnostics.description: Present only when the edit left stops no vehicle can serve.

unitsDeclared.description:
Load units this batch DECLARED on the plan (first upsert naming units
only), in the plan's unit order.

id.description: The row's `id`, when it had one.

error.description: What is wrong and what to send instead.

UpsertRejection.description:
One input row an upsert did not write. `row` is its 0-based index in the
array that was sent — the only handle that works for a row whose `id` is
missing or unusable, which is exactly when this is reported.

summary.description: One host-composed sentence with the counts.

category.description:
`ungeocoded` = rows saved without a location (optimizing is blocked
while a stop or depot uses one). `far_from_plan` = geocoded far from
the rest of the plan — usually a geocoding miss, occasionally
intended.

explanation.description: What this means for the plan, one sentence.

lever.description: The exact call that addresses it (offer it to the user first).

AddressDiagnostics.description:
Address problems the upsert path detected, host-computed (the geocoder and
the geo analysis are black boxes — this block is their only agent-visible
output). Carries counts and next calls, never the rows themselves: the user
sees the affected addresses in the app and in the `fix_addresses` review
dialog, so never enumerate them in chat or in an ask_user question.

summary.description: One host-composed sentence with the counts.

category.description:
`vehicle_incompatible` = stops no vehicle in the fleet can serve
(same name the solver reports post-solve for such stops).

explanation.description: What this means for the plan, one sentence.

lever.description: The exact call that addresses it (offer it to the user first).

FleetDiagnostics.description:
Tag/fleet compatibility problems a data edit left behind, host-computed
from the same predicate the solver applies (required_tags/forbidden_tags
plus the force-allow/deny overrides). Carries counts and next calls, never
the rows: the user sees the affected stops in the app. Absent while the
plan has no vehicles at all — an empty fleet is a normal intermediate
state, not a compatibility problem.

Load units this batch DECLARED on the plan (first upsert naming units

address.description: The `address` as sent (the row's identity, with `area`).

row.description: 0-based index of this row in the `addresses` array that was sent.

matched.description: Canonical address the geocoder matched, when this call geocoded the row.

UpsertAddressesResult.description:
Result of `routing24_upsert_addresses`: the shared upsert counts plus, for
SMALL batches only (at most 5 rows — the confirm-with-the-user use), one
result per input row. `matched` is the canonical address the geocoder
resolved for rows geocoded on this call — state it when confirming a
doubtful address with the user; it is transient and never stored. Rows that
reused an already-located address book entry come back `status: "geocoded"`
with no `matched`. Larger batches return counts and `addressDiagnostics`
only. Rejected rows are NOT in `rows` — they are in `rejected`, under the
same input index.

DeleteByIdsInput.description:
Input for the four `routing24_delete_*` tools: business ids as returned by
the matching `routing24_list_*` (for addresses, the `address` — or
`address, area` — string).

notFound.description: Ids that matched nothing (nothing was deleted for them).

cascade.description:
What was removed alongside (deletes cascade: a depot delete removes
vehicles referencing it; an address delete removes the depots/stops at
it; a stop delete drops its address when nothing else uses it).

fleetDiagnostics.description: Present only when the delete left stops no vehicle can serve.

time_limit_s.description: Solve budget in seconds; omit to auto-scale with problem size.

page.description: The app page to open ("stops" is the Orders page).

id.description: Business id of a stop, depot, or address-book row.

kind.description: `solution` = optimized routes workbook; `plan` = plan data workbook.

plan_id.description: The plan's id, as returned by `routing24_list_plans`.

alreadyLoaded.description: The plan was already the loaded plan; nothing changed.

current.description: Set on the plan currently loaded in the app.

PlanListEntry.description: One saved plan in the `routing24_list_plans` result.

truncated.description: More plans exist beyond this first page of the index.

query.description:
One or more SQLite statements. Statements that write plan data are
rejected — use `routing24_sql_update`.

One or more SQLite statements; UPDATEs on the writable columns of
sites/vehicles/depots journal cell changes that apply atomically.

code.description:
JavaScript/TypeScript for the plan sandbox. Mutate `data` entity
fields; create entities with createSites/createVehicles/createDepots
(rows); delete via deleteSites/deleteVehicles/deleteDepots(predicate);
save a named selection with select(name, rows); assign a short
JSON-serializable summary to `__output`.

rowCount.description: Rows the statement produced (before the wire cap).

noop.description: Set when an UPDATE matched rows but changed nothing.

SqlCell.description: One SQL result cell (bigints arrive as numbers, or strings when unsafe).

noop.description: Set when the statement matched rows but changed nothing.

CommitErrorRow.description: One entity the commit pipeline rejected.

creationsMarked.description: New rows the script authored (createSites/…), before validation.

createdEntities.description: Entities actually created (geocoded + committed with the run).

unitsDeclared.description: Load units this script's created rows newly declared on the plan.

selections.description: Selections the script saved, materialized as sel_* temp tables.

relocatedEntities.description:
Entities relocated by the script writing `address`/`area` (the new
text was re-geocoded; a failed geocode is reported in `warnings`).

sel_table.description: The temp table name (`sel_<name>`), holding one `uuid` column.

sample.description: Up to 5 business ids of the selected rows.

ScriptSelection.description:
One named selection a script saved with `select(name, rows)`, already
materialized as a temp table usable in `routing24_sql_query`.

routes.description:
Draw only these routes (1-based route numbers, as in `routing24_route`)
and fit the frame to them. Everything else — the other routes, their
stops, unassigned pins — is left out, so one route can be read on its
own. Default: the whole plan.

viewport.description: Mirror the user's current map view instead of fitting the plan.

width.description: Image pixels (Retina: 2 device px per CSS px).

fitted.description: What the frame was fitted to.

MapImageResult.description:
Result of `routing24_map_image` (the image itself travels as an MCP image
content block next to this JSON).

since_rev.description:
Change-wait: when set and nothing changed yet, the call holds its reply
(up to the usual ~15s) until the plan's `rev` exceeds this — cheap
push-style notification for a watching agent.

session_id.description:
The session (lane) to read — ids arrive in the `session` echo of
results.

kind.description: Lifecycle lines ('started'/'adopted'/'rehosted') or a tool call.

argsSummary.description: Compact truncated JSON of the call's arguments.

rev.description: Plan drift counter after the call.
